newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Eurofima fixes HK$ bond.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Eurofima fixes HK$ bond.

text.p: Eurofima launched and closed a Hong Kong dollar bond, while Nichimen HK brought a leveraged yen floating rate note to Asian debt markets Friday.

Eurofima, the European Company for Financing of Railroad Stock, launched a six-year HK$400 million bond. The bond, which pays a 7.72 percent coupon semi-annually, was priced at 100.25 to yield 108 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries or 35 basis points over Hong Kong's Exchange Fund Notes.

A syndicate manager at arranger Societe Generale said the high coupon appealed to investors. He said the timing of the issue was based on a view that a tightening by the U.S. Federal Reserve at next week's policymaking meeting could spur some profit-taking in longer-dated U.S. paper, depressing yields.
Lower yields on U.S. paper generally translate into lower yields on Hong Kong paper and that means less investor demand for Hong Kong denominated paper.
Japanese trading company Nichimen launched through its Hong Kong branch a 1.0 billion yen leveraged FRN.

The way the deal is designed, the coupon increases along with the yen LIBOR rate up to a certain point and then goes to zero. It is meant to appeal to investors that expect yen interest rates to rise but not substantially.
Japanese institutional investors are the target.
Arranger Union Bank of Switzerland said today that APP Global Finance's five-year US$500 million floating rate note issue has been oversubscribed by 20-25 percent in syndication.
The borrower has not yet decided whether it will increase the FRN or scale back allotments, UBS said. Allocations are expected to be made on Monday.
Most of the paper was taken by Asian accounts.

The issue size, at US$500 million, is very large for an Asian-targetted deal. Most transactions of that size for Asian borrowers are sold into the U.S. Yankee market, partially on the view that Asian accounts cannot absorb large amounts of paper.
Proceeds of the FRN ultimately will be used by Asia Pulp and Paper.

In other debt news, Philippines Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said the Philippines will work to exempt from a 20 percent withholding tax the soon-to-be-issued uncollateralised bonds offered in exchange for Brady bonds.
Today marks the deadline to submit offers for the exchange.

On Tuesday, arranger J.P. Morgan announced an amendment to the offering that will allow investors making offers for one of the new bonds to switch into the other if their first choice does not attract enough demand to push it over the US$200 million chosen as the minimum amount that will be accepted.
For example, an investor wishing to subscribe to the fixed rate bond has the choice of taking the floating rate note issue if the bond is undersubscribed.
The minimum amounts have been set to assure liquidity in the issues. Acceptance offers will be announced next week.
